newsitem.title: CHINA: China to speed up export tax rebate payment in '97.
newsitem.headline: China to speed up export tax rebate payment in '97.

text.p: China aims to step up the pace of export tax rebate payment in 1997 to try to stimulate exports, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
China had paid 85 billion yuan ($10.24 billion) in export tax rebates in 1996, but still owed 20-30 billion yuan to exporters, the official newspaper said.
"Accelerated clearing of unpaid export rebates will enable state firms to export more," the newspaper said. It did not say how much China expected to pay out in 1997.
Timely payment of the rebates was vital to cash-strapped state-run exporters, already struggling to cope with increased competition, it said.
China's economic growth in 1997 would have to rely largely on exports because domestic demand for consumer and capital goods this year would continue to be weak, it quoted a trade official as saying.
A strong dollar would offset the country's rising foreign exchange reserves and keep the yuan from becoming stronger, the official said.
Lagging imports of capital goods and raw materials would add to growth in foreign exchange reserves, he said, but gave no further details.
